subject: Making Your AI Agents Learn & Remember: Our Latest Session
body:
Hello First Name,

This week's 🦄 ai that works session was all about "Building a Memory Pipeline: Make Your AI Agents Learn & Remember"!

The full recording, code, and diagrams from the session are now available on GitHub:
https://github.com/hellovai/ai-that-works

We dove deep into building memory systems for AI coding agents. The big idea? Moving beyond basic setups to create smart, affordable systems that truly learn from past interactions. Here's a quick recap:

**From Simple to Smart**: We started by showing how to upgrade a basic memory system (think just user/assistant messages) into a much smarter, multi-step pipeline. This new system helps agents capture nuanced details: things like new facts they discover, corrections from humans, and even their own recurring research patterns.

**Smart Savings**: Next, we talked about making these systems affordable. We showed how to use cheaper models, like Jev, for tasks like sorting and filtering data. This frees up more powerful models (like Opus) for the really complex stuff, like synthesizing information and making judgments. It's a great way to keep costs down.

**Build Fast, See Clearly**: Finally, we highlighted the importance of custom tools. We looked at how things like quick testing cycles (using cached LLM requests) and strong observability systems (like BAML Query) are essential for building, debugging, and improving these AI pipelines efficiently.

If you remember one thing from this session: Agent memory isn't a magic prompt. It's an engineered system, a smart pipeline that learns from past interactions, built with custom tools for speed and clarity.

If you have any questions, reply to this email or ask on Discord: https://www.boundaryml.com/discord. We read every message! Happy coding 🧑‍💻

Vaibhav & Dex
